a group of 40 pancreatic and 40 ampullary cancer cases, and the control group was made up of 40 healthy individuals, who were matched for age and gender.

the role of the hematopoiesis-regulating cytokines SCF (stem cell factor), IL-3 (interleukin 3), GM-CSF (granulocyte-macophage-colony-stimulating factor) and M-CSF (macrophage-colony-stiulating factor) as diagnostic markers of pancreatic cancer and their correlation with the most widely used serum markers, CEA (carcinoembryonic-antigen) and CA 19–9.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
M-CSF and IL3 are not reliable biomarkers for pancreatic cancer, and that SCF is a potential biomarker that needs to be further validated.
the diagnostic value of the cytokines is not as great as that of the established pancreatic tumor markers.
the diagnostic value of M-CSF, SCF and IL–3 is not yet fully elucidated and further studies are needed to evaluate the diagnostic value of the combined use with other tumor markers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
M-CSF and GM-CSF are useful in the diagnosis of patients with pancreatic and ampullly cancer.

the serum levels of SCF, M-CSF and IL3 can be used as tumor markers to diagnose patients with pancreatic or ampullary cancer and that the diagnostic sensitivity of SCF and the specificity of M-CSF can be improved by combining their use.
the diagnostic ability of M-SCF and SCF is greater than that of IL-3 and GM-CSF in pancreatic and amullary cancer and the combined use of these markers can improve the diagnostic sensitivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diagnostic sensitivity of M–CSF in pancreatic and Ampullary cancer was higher than that of SCF and the combination of M–CSFs and SCF had higher diagnostic sensitivity.
the diagnostic sensitivity of the combination of M-CSF, SCF and IL–3 is greater than that of CEA, CA 19–9, M-CSF and IL–6, and is equal to that of the combination of CEA, IL–3 and CA 19–19.
